title: Forms V (tafaʿʿala) & VI (tafāʿala)
source: Original instructional lesson authored for this application (syllabus ref: Haywood & Nahmad Ch. 21; Ryding Ch. 26–27)
objectives: Recognize Form V (تَفَعَّلَ) as the reflexive/resultative counterpart of Form II.
Recognize Form VI (تَفَاعَلَ) as the mutual/reciprocal counterpart of Form III.
Identify the distinctive ḍammah before the final radical in Form V/VI maṣādir (تَفَعُّلٌ, تَفَاعُلٌ).
recallPrompt: From Chapter 20: What is the maṣdar pattern of Form II (فَعَّلَ)?

sections.heading: Prefixing تَـ to Forms II and III
sections.body: Form V (تَفَعَّلَ) adds تَـ to Form II, turning a causative action into a reflexive or internal process (عَلَّمَ 'teach' → تَعَلَّمَ 'learn'). Form VI (تَفَاعَلَ) adds تَـ to Form III, expressing mutual or reciprocal action among two or more participants (تَعَاوَنَ 'cooperate').

sections.label: Distinctive Ḍammah in V & VI Maṣādir
sections.summary: Unlike the past stems (which take fatḥah throughout: تَفَعَّلَ, تَفَاعَلَ), the verbal nouns (maṣādir) of Forms V and VI take ḍammah on the second-to-last radical: تَفَعُّلٌ (tafaʿʿul) and تَفَاعُلٌ (tafāʿul).

sections.translation: The students cooperated in learning syntax.
sections.irab: تَعَاوَنَ: فِعْلٌ مَاضٍ (وَزْنُ تَفَاعَلَ) | الطُّلَّابُ: فَاعِلٌ مَرْفُوعٌ | تَعَلُّمِ: مَصْدَرُ الخَامِسِ مَجْرُورٌ بِفِي
sections.notes: Notice how تَعَاوَنَ (Form VI) expresses mutual cooperation, while تَعَلُّمِ (Form V maṣdar) shows the characteristic ḍammah on the doubled lām.

sections.heading: Imperfect Vowels in Forms V & VI
sections.body: Forms V and VI keep fatḥah on the imperfect prefix AND on the middle radical: يَتَفَعَّلُ, يَتَفَاعَلُ (not kasrah!).
